column1: # boru Language Specification: Statement-boundary commit of parked forwards
# The barrier-commit matrix (design/FORWARD-COLLECTION-PHASES.10.md).
# Forward args are gathered in two phases — a plan-time token walk and
# a run-time arrival loop. A word parked for arrivals whose plan filled
# a trailing slot SPECULATIVELY (from the next statement's word) is
# committed when that function word begins its own dispatch, PROVIDED a
# real overload consumes exactly the args it holds. These rows pin the
# whole combination space: boundary kinds × condition shapes × guard
# polarity, the arrival (non-barrier) follows, the explicit silencers,
# the exact-arity commit rule, and the known swallow shapes. Sibling
# rows: control.tsv §6 (the original guard fixes), usurp.tsv (/u as a
# boundary), error.tsv (template messages).
# §1  boundary kinds — a function word starting the next statement
#     commits an else-less guard FIRST; the statement then runs intact.
def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99] def q 1 q
column3: def boundary: guard fires, then the binding statement

column1: def n 5 if (n eq 0) [99] def q 1 q
column3: false guard: binding statement alone

column1: def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99] add 1 2
column3: value-producing boundary: result NOT swallowed as the else

column1: def n 5 if (n eq 0) [99] add 1 2
column3: false guard: the next statement's value survives

column1: def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99] iota 2
column3: builtin generator boundary

column1: def n 5 if (n eq 0) [99] iota 2
column3: false polarity of the same

column1: def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99] for 2 [7]
column3: control-word boundary: the loop runs after the guard

column1: def twice (macro [[e] [ quote [ unquote e add unquote e ] ]]) def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99] twice 5
column3: macro boundary: commit runs before macro expansion

column1: def n 0 if (n eq 0) [raise "zero"] def q (10 div n) q
column3: the guard's raise pre-empts the next statement's div-by-zero

column1: def n 5 if (n eq 0) [raise "zero"] def q (10 div n) q
column3: false guard: the def body computes

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [ if (n eq 0) [raise "zero"] def q (10 div n) q ]] f 0
column3: same shape inside a fn body (the original report)

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [ if (n eq 0) [raise "zero"] def q (10 div n) q ]] f 5
column3: fn-body false polarity

column1: # §2  condition shapes — paren, literal, and def-bound word conditions
#     all park-and-commit the same way (the word-bound condition covers
#     the matcher's deferred /q-preference path).
if true [99] add 1 2
column3: literal true condition

column1: if false [99] add 1 2
column3: literal false condition

column1: def ok true if ok [99] add 1 2
column3: word-bound condition (bestDeferred path carries the speculation)

column1: def ok false if ok [99] add 1 2
column3: word-bound false condition

column1: # §3  plan-claimed stack slots stay plan-consistent — a value BELOW the
#     guard is claimed as the else at plan time (it is not speculative),
#     so true discards it and false yields it.
5 if (1 eq 1) [99] def x 1
column3: a stack value claimed as the else is consumed (true: discarded)

column1: 5 if (1 eq 2) [99] def x 1
column3: …and yielded when the condition is false

column1: # §4  arrivals are NOT barriers — a value-shaped follow fills the else
#     slot exactly as planned: literals, parens, value-def words, type
#     names, templates, and list literals.

column3: a literal after the branches is the else (true: discarded)
…and runs when false
a parenthesised expression is an arrival, not a barrier
…its result is the else

column1: def v 42 if (1 eq 1) [99] v
column3: a value-def word arrives as the else (plan-consistent)

column1: def v 42 if (1 eq 2) [99] v
column3: …and yields its value when false

column1: if (1 eq 1) [99] Integer
column3: a type name arrives as the else

column1: if (1 eq 2) [99] Integer
column3: …and is the result when false
a template string arrives as the else
…evaluated, when false
a list literal after the branches IS the else
…and runs as the else branch when false

column1: # §5  the explicit silencers all behave identically to the commit.
def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99] [] add 1 2
column3: explicit empty else

column1: def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99] end add 1 2
column3: explicit end

column1: def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99] ; add 1 2
column3: ; is end

column1: # §6  the commit needs a REAL overload consuming EXACTLY the claimed
#     args. A boru fn with only a bigger arity keeps waiting for the
#     next statement's result (its synthetic 0-arg fallback must never
#     be committed — that would turn a waiting call into an error), and
#     a smaller real overload fires at the boundary, mirroring the
#     plan-time behaviour of typed overloads.
def g fn [[a:Any b:Any] [Any] [add a b]] g 1 def x 5 x
column3: exact-arity only: 2-arg g cannot commit with one arg and `def` is a barrier — g strands (no wait-through)

column1: def g fn [[a:Any] [Any] [a] [a:Any b:Any] [Any] [add a b]] g 1 def x 5 x
column3: a real smaller overload commits at the boundary

column1: def g fn [[a:Integer] [Integer] [a] [a:Integer b:Integer] [Integer] [add a b]] g 1 def x 5 x
column3: typed overloads resolve the same way at plan time

column1: add 1 def x 5 x
column3: a typed 2-arg native with no smaller overload fails loudly at plan time

column1: # §7  known swallow shapes — value arrivals (§4) mean a guard followed
#     by a pipeline whose FIRST token is a value eats that value as the
#     else; the explicit [] restores the pipeline. Pinned so any change
#     to arrival semantics shows up here loudly.
def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99] [1 2] each [dup mul]
column3: the [1 2] is consumed as the else — each starves

column1: def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99] [] [1 2] each [dup mul]
column3: …the explicit [] keeps the pipeline intact

column1: import "boru:math-util" def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99] [] MathUtil.sqrt 16
column3: module call after a guard needs the [] (the export VALUE would arrive as the else)

column1: import "boru:math-util" def n 5 if (n eq 0) [99] MathUtil.sqrt 16
column3: false polarity: the export lands in the else and the chain proceeds

column1: # §8  chained guards and end-of-program.
def n 0 if (n eq 0) [98] [] if (n eq 0) [99] [] add 1 2
column3: two guards, both silenced explicitly: every result survives

column1: def n 0 if (n eq 0) [98] if (n eq 0) [99] add 1 2
column3: unsilenced chain: the second guard claims the first's 98 as its else (plan-consistent stack claim, §3)

column1: def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99]
column3: end-of-program drains a parked guard: then-branch runs

column1: def n 5 if (n eq 0) [99]
column3: …and a false guard leaves nothing
